_doc: Implicit requirements: what a senior engineer applies without being told, keyed by WORK TYPE (third axis, beside feature kind in edge_cases*.json and scale in scale_tiers.json). An item applies when the declared tier >= from_tier AND the declared risk >= risk (absent = none). class A = always-on default, applied silently and listed as an assumption; B = on from its tier; C = must ask, never defaulted (default is null). blocks_ready marks the C items that may not proceed on an ASSUMED recommendation (docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §5). enforced_by is a runnable `100x ...` or external command, or `review`. Thresholds are quoted from the cited standard, never invented; `scripts/baseline.py lint` rejects an item with no source.

items.default: content reflows at a 320 CSS px wide viewport with no two-dimensional scrolling
items.assumption_text: every view is usable at 320 CSS px width without horizontal scroll
items.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 (2024-12-12) SC 1.4.10 Reflow, Level AA

items.default: text resizes to 200% without loss of content or function
items.assumption_text: font sizes are relative units and layouts survive 200% zoom
items.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 (2024-12-12) SC 1.4.4 Resize Text, Level AA

items.default: text contrast >= 4.5:1, UI component contrast >= 3:1, pointer targets >= 24x24 CSS px
items.assumption_text: colours come from the repo's tokens and meet AA contrast; targets meet the 24px minimum
items.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 (2024-12-12) SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), all Level AA

items.default: every control is keyboard operable, focus is visible and not obscured, and every control has an accessible name and role
items.assumption_text: native elements first; custom widgets carry name, role and value
items.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 (2024-12-12) SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA), SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)

items.default: each view designs loading, empty, error and partial-data states, not only the populated one
items.assumption_text: every data-bound view renders all four states
items.source: Material Design 2 'Empty states' pattern (m2.material.io/design/communication/empty-states.html); ISO/IEC 25010:2023 product quality model, usability and fault-tolerance characteristics

items.default: LCP <= 2.5s, INP <= 200ms, CLS <= 0.1, each at the 75th percentile of page loads
items.assumption_text: public pages are budgeted to the 'good' Core Web Vitals thresholds
items.source: web.dev 'Web Vitals' (web.dev/articles/vitals), 'good' thresholds at p75

items.default: Browserslist `defaults` query (> 0.5%, last 2 versions, Firefox ESR, not dead)
items.assumption_text: the build targets Browserslist `defaults`; anything outside it is ask.unusual-targets
items.source: browserslist/browserslist README, 'Best Practices' and the `defaults` query; owner decision (c)

items.default: a Content-Security-Policy, the standard security response headers, and CSRF protection on every state-changing request when auth is cookie-based
items.assumption_text: CSP and security headers are set by the server; cookie-auth forms carry a CSRF token or rely on SameSite plus origin checks
items.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V3 Web Frontend Security (browser security mechanism headers, cross-site request forgery)

items.default: colours, spacing, radii and type come from the repo's own design system or tokens, never inline literals
items.assumption_text: no new visual values are invented; the repo's tokens are the only source
items.source: owner decision (c); docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §4 tie-break order 2 (repo precedent)

items.default: user-visible strings are externalised and dates, numbers and currency are formatted with the platform locale APIs (Intl on the web)
items.assumption_text: no concatenated user-visible strings; formatting goes through Intl or the platform equivalent
items.source: W3C Internationalization Activity, 'Internationalization Best Practices' (w3.org/International/techniques); ECMA-402 ECMAScript Internationalization API

items.default: respects prefers-color-scheme when the design system ships a dark theme
items.assumption_text: theme follows the OS preference where the tokens provide both themes
items.source: W3C Media Queries Level 5, 'prefers-color-scheme'

items.default: public, indexable pages carry a unique <title>, a meta description and a canonical URL
items.assumption_text: applies to public pages only; authenticated views are noindex
items.source: Google Search Central, 'SEO Starter Guide' (titles, snippets, canonicalization)

items.default: non-essential analytics and tracking load only after opt-in consent
items.assumption_text: analytics is off until the user opts in
items.source: Directive 2002/58/EC (ePrivacy) Art. 5(3); GDPR Art. 4(11) and Art. 7; CJEU C-673/17 Planet49 (pre-ticked boxes are not consent); owner decision (c)

items.default: touch targets >= 44x44 pt on iOS and >= 48x48 dp on Android
items.assumption_text: every tappable element meets the platform minimum
items.source: Apple Human Interface Guidelines, 'Accessibility' (44x44 pt minimum hit target); Material Design 3 'Accessibility: touch targets' (48x48 dp)

items.default: text honours Dynamic Type / sp font scaling, and every control has a screen-reader label
items.assumption_text: layouts survive the largest accessibility text size; VoiceOver and TalkBack announce every control
items.source: Apple HIG 'Typography' (Dynamic Type); Android developer docs 'Accessibility: text scaling' (sp units); W3C WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 and SC 4.1.2

items.default: no orientation lock unless essential; content respects safe areas and insets; layouts adapt to tablet widths
items.assumption_text: both orientations work and nothing renders under notches or system bars
items.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.4 Orientation (AA); Apple HIG 'Layout' (safe areas); Android developer docs 'Display content edge-to-edge'

items.default: every network action has a defined offline and timeout behaviour; reads show cached data, writes queue or fail visibly
items.assumption_text: no spinner that never ends; lost connectivity is a designed state
items.source: Android developer docs, 'Build an offline-first app' (developer.android.com/topic/architecture/data-layer/offline-first)

items.default: user-perceived crash rate < 1.09% and user-perceived ANR rate < 0.47% overall (28-day average)
items.assumption_text: release health is tracked against Google Play's bad-behaviour thresholds
items.source: Android developer docs, 'Android vitals' (developer.android.com/topic/performance/vitals), core vitals bad behaviour thresholds

items.default: store release is staged (Play staged rollout / App Store phased release) and the feature has a remote kill switch
items.assumption_text: a bad build can be halted, and a bad feature disabled without a new binary
items.source: Google Play Console Help, 'Release app updates with staged rollouts'; App Store Connect Help, 'Release a version update in phases'

items.default: iOS privacy manifest declares required-reason APIs and data collection; every runtime permission is requested in context with a rationale
items.assumption_text: permissions are asked at point of use, never at launch
items.source: Apple Developer docs, 'Privacy manifest files'; Android developer docs, 'Request runtime permissions' (shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale)

items.ask: Which minimum iOS / Android versions and which device classes (phone, tablet, foldable) must be supported?
items.source: docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §5 class C (unusual device targets)

items.default: object-level and function-level authorization checked on every endpoint, server-side, from the authenticated identity
items.assumption_text: no endpoint trusts a client-supplied owner, tenant or role id
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API1 Broken Object Level Authorization, API5 Broken Function Level Authorization

items.default: request bodies bind to an allowlisted DTO; responses expose only fields the caller may read
items.assumption_text: unknown fields are rejected; no model is spread from request input
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization

items.default: every input is validated at the trust boundary for type, range, length and format, with explicit size limits
items.assumption_text: validation happens before business logic, not inside it
items.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2 Validation and Business Logic

items.default: list endpoints have a maximum page size; request bodies and uploads have a maximum size
items.assumption_text: no unbounded list or body
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

items.default: per-client rate limiting at the gateway, returning 429 with Retry-After
items.assumption_text: rate limiting sits at the gateway; app-level counters remain for lockout
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption; RFC 6585 §4 (429 Too Many Requests)

items.default: errors use RFC 9457 problem details and never leak stack traces or internal identifiers
items.assumption_text: one error shape across the API; stack traces stay in logs
items.source: IETF RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs; OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V16 Security Logging and Error Handling

items.default: unsafe retried operations accept an idempotency key; every outbound call has a timeout; retries are bounded with backoff
items.assumption_text: no outbound call without a timeout; no unbounded retry
items.source: Google SRE book ch. 22 'Addressing Cascading Failures' (timeouts, deadlines, limiting retries)

items.default: separate liveness and readiness endpoints; SIGTERM drains in-flight work before exit
items.assumption_text: deploys do not drop in-flight requests
items.source: The Twelve-Factor App, IX Disposability; Kubernetes docs 'Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes'

items.default: the OpenAPI or protobuf contract is checked in and linted in CI
items.assumption_text: the contract is the source of truth for clients
items.source: OpenAPI Specification 3.1.0; OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API9 Improper Inventory Management

items.default: any server-side fetch of a user-supplied URL uses an allowlist and blocks private, loopback and metadata addresses
items.assumption_text: no server-side fetch of an arbitrary user URL
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API7 Server Side Request Forgery

items.default: an inventory of API versions and hosts, with a stated deprecation and sunset policy
items.assumption_text: old versions are retired on a schedule, not left running
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API9 Improper Inventory Management; IETF RFC 8594 (Sunset header)

items.default: handlers are idempotent because delivery is at-least-once
items.assumption_text: a redelivered message produces no second side effect
items.source: AWS SQS Developer Guide, 'Amazon SQS standard queues' (at-least-once delivery; design idempotent consumers)

items.default: retries use capped exponential backoff with jitter, then move to a dead-letter queue
items.assumption_text: a poison message lands in the DLQ instead of looping
items.source: AWS Builders' Library, 'Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter'; AWS SQS Developer Guide, 'Using dead-letter queues'

items.default: the visibility timeout (or lease) exceeds the handler's maximum runtime
items.assumption_text: a slow handler is not redelivered to a second worker mid-run
items.source: AWS SQS Developer Guide, 'Amazon SQS visibility timeout'

items.default: alerts on queue depth and oldest-message age, not only on errors
items.assumption_text: a stalled consumer pages someone before users notice
items.source: Google SRE book ch. 6 'Monitoring Distributed Systems' (saturation, symptom-based alerting)

items.default: scheduled jobs forbid overlapping runs, define missed-run behaviour, and state their time zone explicitly
items.assumption_text: a slow run never overlaps the next; schedules are not tied to the host's local time
items.source: Kubernetes docs 'CronJob' (concurrencyPolicy, startingDeadlineSeconds, timeZone)

items.default: each run writes whole partitions idempotently so any partition can be re-run or backfilled
items.assumption_text: re-running a day replaces that day, never appends a duplicate
items.source: Google SRE workbook ch. 13 'Data Processing Pipelines' (idempotent, re-runnable stages)

items.default: message and dataset schemas are versioned with a declared compatibility rule
items.assumption_text: producers cannot break consumers with an incompatible schema change
items.source: Apache Avro 1.12 specification, 'Schema Resolution'; Protocol Buffers docs, 'Updating A Message Type'

items.default: each stage asserts row counts, null rates and key uniqueness, and fails the run when they break
items.assumption_text: bad data stops the pipeline instead of propagating
items.source: Google SRE workbook ch. 13 'Data Processing Pipelines' (data correctness monitoring)

items.default: event-time windows with watermarks and a stated allowed-lateness
items.assumption_text: late events are handled by rule, not dropped silently
items.source: Akidau et al., 'The Dataflow Model', PVLDB 8(12), 2015

items.ask: Which datasets carry personal data, and where may each copy of it flow?
items.source: GDPR Art. 30 (records of processing); Japan APPI (Act on the Protection of Personal Information) Art. 27-30 (third-party provision records)

items.default: --help works, failure exits non-zero, data goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr, NO_COLOR disables colour
items.assumption_text: the CLI composes in pipes and scripts
items.source: Command Line Interface Guidelines (clig.dev); no-color.org (NO_COLOR environment variable)

items.default: releases are versioned with SemVer and recorded in a CHANGELOG
items.assumption_text: a breaking flag change bumps the major version
items.source: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (semver.org); Keep a Changelog 1.1.0

items.default: minimal dependencies, each vetted, with a committed lockfile
items.assumption_text: every new dependency is vetted before it is added
items.source: NIST SP 800-218 SSDF v1.1 PW.4 (reuse existing, well-secured software) and PS.3.2 (component provenance)

items.default: no publicly accessible storage bucket or database; encryption at rest on every data store
items.assumption_text: public access is blocked by default at the account level
items.source: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v5.0.0 §2.1.4 (S3 Block Public Access), §2.2.1 (RDS encryption at rest); equivalent controls in the CIS GCP and Azure benchmarks

items.default: least-privilege IAM: no wildcard admin policies on workloads, no long-lived user keys where roles exist
items.assumption_text: each workload has its own narrowly scoped role
items.source: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v5.0.0 §1 Identity and Access Management

items.default: automated backups on, and a restore is actually performed on a schedule to prove them
items.assumption_text: an untested backup is treated as no backup
items.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Reliability pillar REL09-BP04 'Perform periodic recovery of the data to verify backup integrity and processes'; Google SRE book ch. 26 'Data Integrity'

items.default: infrastructure state lives in a remote backend with locking
items.assumption_text: two applies cannot run against the same state concurrently
items.source: HashiCorp Terraform docs, 'State: Locking' and 'Backends'

items.default: every resource carries cost-allocation tags, and a budget alert exists for the account or project
items.assumption_text: unexpected spend alerts someone before the invoice does
items.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Cost Optimization pillar COST02 (governance, budgets) and COST03 (cost allocation tagging)

items.default: stateful services deploy across multiple availability zones with automatic failover
items.assumption_text: one zone failing does not take the service down
items.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Reliability pillar REL10 'Use fault isolation to protect your workload'

items.default: a multi-region topology with a documented failover procedure
items.assumption_text: cross-region latency is budgeted explicitly
items.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Reliability pillar REL10 and REL13 (plan for disaster recovery)

items.default: no secrets in code or config files; secrets come from the environment or a secret manager, and secret scanning runs on every push
items.assumption_text: credentials never enter version control
items.source: The Twelve-Factor App, III Config; OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13 Configuration (secret management)

items.default: SAST in CI, automated dependency update PRs, and third-party CI actions pinned by commit SHA
items.assumption_text: the pipeline cannot be changed by a moved tag
items.source: NIST SP 800-218 SSDF v1.1 PW.7 (review/analyse code) and PW.8 (test executable code); OpenSSF Scorecard checks SAST, Dependency-Update-Tool, Pinned-Dependencies

items.default: release artifacts ship with an SBOM and build provenance
items.assumption_text: consumers can verify what was built and from what
items.source: SLSA v1.0 Build track (provenance); NIST SP 800-218 SSDF v1.1 PS.3 (archive each release with provenance data)

items.default: the spec's security section names the assets, the trust boundaries crossed and the top abuse cases
items.assumption_text: a short threat model is written before code
items.source: NIST SP 800-218 SSDF v1.1 PW.1.1 (threat modeling to inform design)

items.default: personal data, credentials and session tokens are never written to logs, traces or error reports
items.assumption_text: logging redacts by allowlist, not by hope
items.source: GDPR Art. 25 (data protection by design and by default) and Art. 5(1)(c) (data minimisation); OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V16

items.default: latency, traffic, errors and saturation are measured; logs are structured; trace context propagates across hops
items.assumption_text: a failing request can be followed end to end
items.source: Google SRE book ch. 6 'Monitoring Distributed Systems' (four golden signals); W3C Trace Context Recommendation; OpenTelemetry specification

items.default: every paging alert links a runbook that says what to check and how to mitigate
items.assumption_text: an alert without a runbook is not shipped
items.source: Google SRE book ch. 11 'Being On-Call' (playbooks) and ch. 6 (every page must be actionable)

items.default: tests ship in the same change as the code, and they are deterministic (no sleeps, no wall-clock, no network)
items.assumption_text: no 'tests in a follow-up'
items.source: Google Engineering Practices, 'What to look for in a code review' (Tests) (google.github.io/eng-practices)

items.default: an end-to-end test covers each critical user journey, and only those
items.assumption_text: a few e2e tests on the money paths; everything else lower in the pyramid
items.source: Google Testing Blog, 'Just Say No to More End-to-End Tests' (2015-04-22)

items.default: screenshot comparison on the shared components and key screens
items.assumption_text: unintended visual change is caught in CI
items.source: Playwright docs, 'Visual comparisons' (toHaveScreenshot); tier gating inferred

items.default: load, soak and spike tests before a capacity-relevant release
items.assumption_text: capacity claims are measured, not projected
items.source: Google SRE book ch. 17 'Testing for Reliability' (load and stress testing); scripts/data/scale_tiers.json growth.required

items.default: risky behaviour ships behind a feature flag, and the rollback step is written and has been executed once
items.assumption_text: turning it off is one action, and that action is known to work
items.source: Google SRE workbook ch. 16 'Canarying Releases'; Google SRE book ch. 8 'Release Engineering'

items.default: releases go to a canary population first, gated on error and latency comparison
items.assumption_text: a bad release reaches a small slice before everyone
items.source: Google SRE workbook ch. 16 'Canarying Releases'

items.default: work lands as small, self-contained changes
items.assumption_text: a large feature is split into reviewable slices
items.source: Google Engineering Practices, 'Small CLs' (google.github.io/eng-practices/review/developer/small-cls.html)

items.default: the README states how to run and test; architecturally significant choices are recorded as ADRs
items.assumption_text: a newcomer can run the tests from the README alone
items.source: Michael Nygard, 'Documenting Architecture Decisions' (2011); research/21-findings-agent-instruction-corpus.md (one named prove-it command)

items.default: timestamps stored in UTC (RFC 3339 on the wire), zones from the IANA tz database, DST transitions tested, text handled as Unicode with normalisation where compared
items.assumption_text: no local-time storage; no byte-length assumptions on text
items.source: IETF RFC 3339; IANA Time Zone Database; Unicode Standard Annex #15 (Normalization Forms)

items.default: a dependency under a copyleft licence (GPL, AGPL, LGPL, MPL, EPL family) is flagged for licence review before adoption
items.assumption_text: copyleft is a review flag, not an automatic rejection
items.source: SPDX License List (spdx.org/licenses); owner decision (c)

items.default: WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the floor at every tier
items.assumption_text: AA conformance is not traded away for speed at any tier
items.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 (2024-12-12) conformance Level AA; owner decision (c)

items.default: security-relevant events (auth, permission change, data export, admin action) are written to a tamper-evident audit log
items.assumption_text: who did what, when, is reconstructible
items.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V16 Security Logging and Error Handling; PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 10

items.default: a data protection impact assessment is written before launch and linked from the spec's privacy section
items.assumption_text: regulated processing is assessed before it starts, not after an incident
items.source: GDPR Art. 35 (data protection impact assessment)

items.default: TLS 1.2+ on every hop that carries personal or credential data, including internal service-to-service
items.assumption_text: no plaintext hop for sensitive data, inside the network or out
items.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12 Secure Communication

items.ask: In which country or region must personal data be stored and processed?
items.source: GDPR Chapter V (Art. 44-49, transfers to third countries); Japan APPI Art. 28 (provision to third parties in foreign countries)

items.ask: How long is each class of personal data kept, and what deletes it?
items.source: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) (storage limitation); Japan APPI Art. 22 (deletion when no longer needed)

items.ask: Which legal or contractual regime applies (GDPR, APPI, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, none)?
items.source: docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §5 class C (compliance regime); GDPR; Japan APPI; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; PCI DSS v4.0.1

items.ask: What recurring spend may this add (a monthly ceiling, or 'existing infrastructure only')?
items.source: docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §4 (recurring cost is a one-way door) and §5 (money is class C)

items.ask: How much data may be lost (RPO) and how long may the service be down (RTO) after a disaster?
items.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Reliability pillar REL13-BP01 'Define recovery objectives for downtime and data loss'

items.ask: What availability and latency SLOs does this product commit to?
items.source: Google SRE workbook ch. 2 'Implementing SLOs' (SLOs are a product decision)

items.ask: Must any browser, device or OS outside the defaults (Browserslist `defaults`, current and previous major OS) be supported?
items.source: docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §5 class C (unusual device targets)

items.ask: Which locales and languages ship at launch, and is any right-to-left?
items.source: W3C Internationalization Activity, 'Internationalization Best Practices'

items.ask: Is this multi-tenant, and is isolation by row, schema, database or deployment?
items.source: AWS SaaS Lens (Well-Architected), 'Silo, pool and bridge models'; OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API1

items.ask: Is this API public (third parties, versioned contract) or internal (own clients only)?
items.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023: API9 Improper Inventory Management; docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md §4 (public API shape is a one-way door)
